prerequisites: Students must have passed all other subjects in the study plan and have all credits required to obtain the Degree title, except those corresponding to the TFG itself.

learning_outcomes.text: Realization of an original project, individually or in a group, in the field of technology specific to the Degree, of a professional nature, synthesizing and integrating the acquired competencies.
All general or transversal competencies (CG1 to CG15) indicated in the verification report will be worked on, as well as the specific competence associated with the TFG.
Capacity to integrate all general and specific competencies within the scope of the completed Degree studies.
Concrete learning outcomes will vary depending on the topic assigned by the tutor, but generally will be directly related to the specific objectives of the degree.

These results will be reflected in the individual or group completion of the work, presentation, and individual defense before a university committee of an original project in the field of Engineering of a professional nature, synthesizing and integrating all acquired competencies.

syllabus_topics: The contents of the End-of-Degree Project carried out individually by each student will be framed within one of the work topics included in the area of Engineering in which they have pursued their studies, as indicated in the objectives of each degree.

assessment_methods.method: Monitoring of student's in-person activities by their academic tutor
Final document presented by the student
Public presentation of the work before the committee and subsequent debate

assessment_rules: The End-of-Degree Project must be presented and defended before a university committee. The evaluation will generally consider the monitoring of the student's in-person activities by their academic tutor, the final document presented by the student, and the public presentation and debate before the committee. The final definition of the evaluation system will comply with the regulations defined in the School of Engineering's End-of-Degree Project Regulation. Both ordinary and extraordinary evaluations are conducted through a public presentation before a committee of three professors. Although the work may be part of a joint effort, the presentation must be individual, clearly highlighting each student's specific contributions.
